races.name: Boodles Anniversary 4-Y-O Juvenile Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Maestro Conti
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with highest RPR who has won his last three starts and suits the likely tactical scenario perfectly
runners_data.comment: Travelled smoothly for a long way when runner-up in the Triumph last month; key player
runners_data.spotlight: Untroubled to win sole start in France and scored in good style at Kempton (2m, good) and Cheltenham (Grade 2) in first two runs for Dan Skelton; well backed into 5-1 when runner-up in the Triumph Hurdle at Cheltenham (2m1f, soft) last month, when he travelled smoothly for a long way before keeping on well to edge out Minella Study in the battle for second; has leading claims on that form and he should be unfazed by this return to a sharper track.

runners_data.name: Mange Tout
runners_data.note: Reliable prominent performer but 66 days off and may need this run despite her excellent record fresh
runners_data.comment: Third in Grade 1 at Leopardstown but was behind Selma De Vary and needs to resume progress
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to multiple Grade 1 winner Impaire Et Passe; won her first three starts over hurdles before a third in Grade 1 at Leopardstown (2m, heavy) in February; may have more to offer in this sphere but she finished behind Selma De Vary last time and needs to resume progress.

runners_data.name: Selma De Vary
runners_data.note: French import with solid form but may find this level too sharp after a promising but unspectacular British debut
runners_data.comment: Got hampered in closing stages when fourth in the Triumph; big player for Willie Mullins
runners_data.spotlight: Ran twice on Flat in France and three times in hurdle races at Auteuil, culminating in a win in November (2m1f, heavy); made a promising start for new yard when runner-up behind Narciso Has in a Grade 1 at Leopardstown in February; didn't come from so far back when fourth in the Triumph at Cheltenham last month but she made smooth progress and kept on well after being hampered in the closing stages; that makes her one of the form picks in this field and Willie Mullins has won this twice in the last three years.

runners_data.name: Indian River
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who was exposed at Grade 1 level last time and faces a tactical disadvantage here
runners_data.comment: Triple hurdle winner but his limitations were exposed in the Triumph (tenth) last month
runners_data.spotlight: Promise in his two Irish Flat maidens; justified favouritism in first three starts over hurdles but his limitations were exposed when a never-dangerous tenth in the Triumph at Cheltenham (50-1) last month; passed over.

runners_data.name: Aqua Bleu
runners_data.note: Willing front-runner but all wins have come at lower levels and may struggle to sustain pace against this class
runners_data.comment: Front-runner who is 3-4 over hurdles but he has a lot to find in this Grade 1 contest
runners_data.spotlight: Promising second on debut at Hereford (2m, good) in November and he's unbeaten in three runs since; has looked a very willing front-runner but all his wins have been in small-field events and he has a lot to find in this Grade 1 contest.

runners_data.name: Winston Junior
runners_data.note: Learning to settle better but still has prominent tendencies that could see him caught in traffic
runners_data.comment: Second in the juvenile handicap at Cheltenham and he's open to more progress; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: Useful maiden on the Flat at up 1m5f and he has a record of 2212 since switched to hurdling for his current yard; seems to be learning to settle better and he didn't get a smooth run when an eye-catching second in the juvenile handicap at Cheltenham (2m, good to soft) last month; that was another good step forward and he could continue to progress in this sphere; interesting contender.

runners_data.name: Wolf Rayet
runners_data.note: Ran well in Triumph at big odds but was beaten favourite last time and hold-up style doesn't suit likely pace
runners_data.comment: Ran well at a massive price in the Triumph but beaten 10l and he was behind three of these
runners_data.spotlight: Three Flat runs in Ireland and four over hurdles in Britain; ran well at a massive price in the Triumph at Cheltenham (eighth of 20) last month but he was beaten 10l and finished behind three of today's rivals; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Ammes
runners_data.note: Decent record but hasn't won since early career and 30 days off may have him needing the run
runners_data.comment: Listed runner-up but he was well held in the juvenile handicap at Cheltenham last month
runners_data.spotlight: Good Flat horse who won his first two starts over hurdles before a close second behind Minella Study in a Listed race at Wetherby (2m, good) in October; still has potential in this sphere but he was only 12th in the juvenile handicap at Cheltenham last month and needs to resume his progress in this tough race; visor added.

runners_data.name: Lord
runners_data.note: Proven course winner who can lead but 68 days off is a concern against sharper rivals
runners_data.comment: 4-7 over hurdles but this is a tough test and he has plenty to find on the figures
runners_data.spotlight: Made it 4-6 over hurdles when returning to form with an all-the-way win in a Listed event over C&D (soft) in December; ran to a similar level when runner-up in the Scottish Triumph at Musselburgh in January but this is a much tougher test and he has plenty to find on the figures; cheekpieces added.

runners_data.name: Minella Study
runners_data.note: High-class performer who ran well in Triumph and has the tactical speed to position well
runners_data.comment: Close third in the Triumph when he split Maestro Conti and Selma De Vary; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Six-race maiden on the Flat but he's 3-4 over hurdles and travelled strongly for a long way when close third in the Triumph at Cheltenham last month; split Maestro Conti and Selma De Vary in that race and should make another bold bid here; that last run was on soft but his second win was on good.

races.paceDynamic: Lord and Aqua Bleu will ensure a genuine pace from the start, with both confirmed front-runners likely to dispute the early lead over the opening circuit. The prominent brigade of Maestro Conti, Mange Tout, Selma De Vary, and Winston Junior will create significant traffic problems turning for home, particularly with four horses wanting similar positions 2-3 out. Hold-up horses Indian River and Wolf Rayet face the dual challenge of getting a clear run and making up significant ground against proven Grade-level performers who can sustain their efforts. This pace dynamic strongly favours prominent racers who can secure good positions early and avoid the inevitable squeeze.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Takes Charge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is solid but not frantic, allowing the prominent runners to track comfortably
scenarios.body: Maestro Conti or Minella Study can use their class edge to strike turning in, benefiting from the perfect stalking position behind the leaders. Their superior ratings and recent Grade-level form gives them the tactical advantage when the race develops.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Lord or Aqua Bleu can dictate at a manageable tempo without serious early pressure
scenarios.body: The leader gets first run and holds off late challengers, with their stamina proven at this trip on testing ground. Soft conditions suit both front-runners' previous winning performances.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Charge Success
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses early or traffic opens up perfectly for the back markers
scenarios.body: Indian River or Wolf Rayet get the ideal setup with a moderate pace and clear passage, allowing their finishing kick to be effective. Their hold-up style only works if the race falls apart tactically.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Meltdown
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too hard early and the prominent runners get caught in traffic
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery with tired leaders and blocked prominent runners, creating opportunities for any horse getting a clear run. Tactical positioning becomes irrelevant in a scrimmaging finish.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic problems at the second-last flight where Mange Tout, Winston Junior, and Selma De Vary could all converge on the same piece of ground
Monitor how aggressively Lord and Aqua Bleu go in the early stages as both have front-running tendencies that could create a pace duel
Indian River and Wolf Rayet need the race to develop perfectly with either slow early pace or clear late runs to be competitive
Maestro Conti has been well-backed and Harry Skelton's positioning will be crucial given the likely prominent congestion
The 66-day gap for Mange Tout could be significant despite Elliott's excellent record with horses returning from breaks

races.name: William Hill Manifesto Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Lulamba
runners_data.note: Front runner with proven Grade 1 class despite Arkle third, but faces another confirmed leader in Jax Junior which could compromise his tactics
runners_data.comment: Beaten favourite in the Arkle; has otherwise been a rising star; this new trip should suit
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on any ground; ran creditably on the figures but was only third when favourite for the Arkle, in which a mistake two out cost him some ground when challenging; has otherwise been a rising force at about 2m and his record away from the Cheltenham Festival is 6-6, comfortably beating his elders in the Game Spirit for the most recent success; gives the firm impression he's ready for a crack at this new trip; sets the standard and retains the potential for rating higher still.

runners_data.name: Blueking d'Oroux
runners_data.note: Prominent racer wearing cheekpieces who benefits from the likely strong pace, though Paul Nicholls' moderate 14-day form is a slight concern
runners_data.comment: Won a substandard Rising Stars; close second in handicap last time; this is a stiffer task
runners_data.spotlight: Useful 2m4f novice chaser but he won a substandard edition of the Rising Stars at Wincanton and his close second at Kempton (with cheekpieces fitted) last time was achieved in a handicap; faces a stiffer task at this level in the retained headgear.

runners_data.name: Koktail Divin
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose stamina was proven in the Brown Advisory, making the return to 2m4f potentially ideal for his profile
runners_data.comment: Non-stayer in the 3m1f Brown Advisory; broadly progressive otherwise; remains of interest
runners_data.spotlight: Non-stayer (shaped better than the bare result) in the 3m1f Brown Advisory at Cheltenham having surprisingly swerved the 2m4f Jack Richards option; broadly progressive otherwise and scored by a wide margin at Leopardstown (2m5f, yielding) the time before, recording a very useful RPR; ran well in the Mersey over hurdles at this meeting 12 months ago; remains of major interest, back down in distance.

runners_data.name: Jax Junior
runners_data.note: Front runner wearing a tongue-tie who finished well behind Lulamba in the Arkle but should appreciate this step back up in trip
runners_data.comment: Has a good strike-rate when racing beyond 2m, the most recent success in Kempton Grade 2
runners_data.spotlight: Finished 18l behind Lulamba in the Arkle but may fare better in this rematch, with the return to further a likely plus; readily bagged Grade 2 honours at Kempton (2m4f, good to soft) the time before, enhancing his good strike-rate when racing beyond 2m.

runners_data.name: Mambonumberfive
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning fresh after 61 days who faces a tactical disadvantage given the likely strong early pace from two front runners
runners_data.comment: Best to forgive latest effort; 3-3 over fences otherwise; may resume improvement; new trip
runners_data.spotlight: Comes here fresh having bypassed the Cheltenham Festival and been absent since a Kingmaker defeat that is perhaps best forgiven due to the heavy ground; 3-3 over fences otherwise, including 2m wins at Aintree (handicap) and Kempton (Grade 2, readily); may resume improvement, provided he stays the new trip.

races.paceDynamic: Lulamba and Jax Junior are both confirmed front runners who will set a genuine gallop from the start, with neither likely to yield easily in the early stages. This creates an honest pace throughout the 2m4f trip, preventing any slow early fractions that could favor hold-up horses. The prominent racers Blueking d'Oroux and Koktail Divin will track the leaders closely, while Mambonumberfive faces the toughest task from his hold-up position. This pace setup clearly favors the prominent racers who can sit just off the pace and strike when the front runners tire.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Lulamba and Jax Junior duel too hard early and weaken in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The honest gallop set by the front runners plays into the hands of those tracking just behind, allowing them to time their runs perfectly. Blueking d'Oroux and Koktail Divin benefit most from this tactical setup with their preferred prominent positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lulamba Dominates Again
scenarios.trigger: If Lulamba can dictate terms from the front without facing serious early pressure
scenarios.body: Despite Jax Junior's presence, Lulamba's superior class tells as he controls the pace and kicks clear approaching the last. His Arkle third shows he belongs at this level, and the slight step up in trip suits his stamina reserves.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Distance Specialists Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly searching and stamina becomes the deciding factor
scenarios.body: The 2m4f trip and testing ground combine to expose the lesser stayers in the field. Koktail Divin's recent 3m1f Brown Advisory run suggests he has untapped stamina reserves for this intermediate distance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Shock Fresh Horse
scenarios.trigger: If Mambonumberfive's 61-day break proves an advantage and the pace collapses early
scenarios.body: The hold-up horse benefits from superior fitness while others have had harder recent campaigns. His fresh legs and proven 2m ability could surprise if the early pace is moderate enough to give him a chance.

watchPoints.text: Lulamba and Jax Junior could engage in a pace duel that destroys both their chances early in the race
Mambonumberfive may struggle to get competitive from his hold-up style if the early pace is as strong as expected
Blueking d'Oroux's cheekpieces could sharpen his jumping which was his main weakness in previous defeats
Koktail Divin's last run was 29 days ago in testing conditions which may have left its mark
Tom Cannon's 7lb claim on Jax Junior provides a useful weight advantage in this competitive field

races.name: Racing Welfare Bowl Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Pic d'Orhy
runners_data.note: Front-runner with 54 days since last run who showed his class against Jonbon at Ascot and will relish controlling the pace in this small field
runners_data.comment: 11yo; three Grade 1 wins (including here); looked as good as ever last time; not ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: 11yo who looked as good as ever when runner-up in a captivating battle with Jonbon in the Ascot Chase (2m5f, good to soft) in February, when bidding to win that Grade 1 for the third consecutive year; won the Grade 1 Melling Chase here (2m4f, soft) in 2023; seemed fine at 3m when 1l second in this season's Charlie Hall (good) and his trainer has won this race six times; no surprise to see a bold bid from this front-runner, who is not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Impaire Et Passe
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse stepping up significantly in trip after his Cheltenham pull-up, though his Aintree record suggests the track suits
runners_data.comment: Pulled up in the Ryanair but 2-2 at this meeting and could bounce back with a big run
runners_data.spotlight: Unproven at this trip and reportedly never travelling when pulled up in the Ryanair at Cheltenham last month; however, he's won at this meeting in each of the last two seasons, landing the Grade 1 Manifesto Novices' Chase last April (2m4f, good to soft; Jango Baie third), and he produced a top performance in the Grade 2 Red Mills Chase at Gowran Park this February; could bounce back with big run for last year's winning trainer Willie Mullins.

runners_data.name: Jango Baie
runners_data.note: Prominent racer improving for longer distances this season who can track the leader and time his challenge from an ideal position
runners_data.comment: Runner-up in the Gold Cup; leading claims if that hard race 27 days ago hasn't left a mark
runners_data.spotlight: Kept on for close third to Impaire Et Passe in the 2m4f Manifesto here 12 months ago and has improved for longer trips this season; very close fourth in thrilling finish to the King George at Kempton (3m, good) in December and 8l second in the Gold Cup at Cheltenham (3m2f, good to soft) last month; leading claims if that hard race 27 days ago hasn't left a mark.

runners_data.name: Spillane's Tower
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner having his first start for 75 days with trainer James Mangan having limited recent form but the trip should suit
runners_data.comment: Probably something in tank (travelled up strongly to take over) for Cheltenham Grade 2 win
runners_data.spotlight: Won two Irish Grade 1s in the spring of 2024 as a novice and a Grade 2 at Cheltenham (near 3m2f, soft) this January; while he does not look the best handicapped, this 8yo probably had something in the tank last time (he travelled up strongly to take over) and could have been building to something special this spring; withdrawn from the Gold Cup on raceday due to unsuitable ground; also declared for Thursday's Grade 1.

runners_data.name: Protektorat
runners_data.note: Prominent 11-year-old who showed he retains ability when second to Jonbon here last year and can race handily throughout
runners_data.comment: 11yo; no Grade 1 win since March 2024 but still capable of strong form; possible contender
runners_data.spotlight: 11yo whose last Grade 1 win came in March 2024 but he showed strong form when keeping on for second of four to Jonbon in the Melling Chase here (2m4f, good) 12 months ago and has won at Windsor (2m6f, soft; warm conditions race) and Kelso (extended 2m7f, good to soft; Listed) on his two runs this year; he should still be fine at this sort of trip and could be a contender.

races.paceDynamic: Pic d'Orhy will take them along from the front at a sustainable gallop, with Jango Baie and Protektorat likely to track him in behind. The small field and lack of genuine pace pressure means this will develop into a staying test rather than a speed battle. Hold-up horses Impaire Et Passe and Spillane's Tower will need to rely on stamina and finishing kick from the back. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can dictate terms and have the stamina to see out the extended trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pic d'Orhy Dominates Front
scenarios.trigger: If Pic d'Orhy gets an uncontested lead and maintains rhythm
scenarios.body: His class and front-running style will be perfectly suited to controlling this small field. The 11-year-old's stamina reserves will prove decisive when others struggle with the pace injection late on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Jango Baie or Protektorat can travel smoothly behind the leader
scenarios.body: Either prominent runner can time their challenge perfectly from an ideal stalking position. Their ability to stay in touch without doing early work gives them the tactical edge over the hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up Horse Comeback
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Impaire Et Passe's class could shine through if the race becomes tactical enough for his finishing kick. The trip remains a concern but his raw ability might overcome positional disadvantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Spillane's Tower Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the recent Grade 2 winner finds significant improvement for the step up in trip
scenarios.body: His 75-day break might have him primed for a big effort at a longer distance that suits. The extended trip could unlock untapped stamina reserves that his connections believe exist.

watchPoints.text: Impaire Et Passe looks vulnerable if the pace is genuine early as his hold-up style and trip question create a double tactical disadvantage
Pic d'Orhy's 54-day break could leave him short of peak fitness if the race becomes a grueling stamina test in the closing stages
Jango Baie's positioning will be crucial - if he gets too keen tracking Pic d'Orhy he could compromise his finishing kick
Spillane's Tower's 75-day absence and trainer's poor recent record suggest he needs to find significant improvement to feature
The genuine good to soft going favors the entire field based on their recent form patterns and preferences

races.name: Randox Foxhunters' Open Hunters' Chase

runners_data.name: Gaboriot
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who pulled up here in December and has disappointed since, headgear change may help
runners_data.comment: Return to form needed but twice placed over these fences and gets a change of headgear
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up in the Becher here in December and his two subsequent hunter chase runs have yielded an early fall and disappointing defeat; twice placed over these fences, however, most recently in the Grand Sefton over C&D in November, and could have an each-way shout if back on song in change of headgear.

runners_data.name: Thunder Rock
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the expected pace scenario perfectly, Olly Murphy's 9/28 record concerning
runners_data.comment: Very talented in his prime; easy hunter chase wins on last two starts; could be in the mix
runners_data.spotlight: Very talented in his prime; this 10yo isn't the force of old and today's race is much tougher than the hunter chases he's won easily on his last two starts (2m4f, good to soft/good) but if he can tap further into his back-class he may well be in the mix; James King has won this twice.

runners_data.name: Its On The Line
runners_data.note: Defending champion with prominent style, excellent soft going record but faces traffic dangers
runners_data.comment: Won this in 2024; went close again at Cheltenham last month and he's entitled to respect
runners_data.spotlight: Won this in 2024 (heavy); beaten a neck by Barton Snow at last month's Cheltenham Festival (3m2f, good to soft), finishing a close second in that hunter chase for the fourth season in a row; at this trip he may prefer more testing ground than is likely today, but he's still entitled to respect.

runners_data.name: Java Point
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid recent hunter chase form, headgear first time
runners_data.comment: 11yo who has been in good form since tackling hunter chases but needs a bigger run today
runners_data.spotlight: Useful, four-time handicap chase winner who scored at Ludlow (3m, good to soft) in January on his first hunter chase start; runner-up on next two outings (3m/2m7f, soft/good to soft); this 11yo needs a bigger run today.

runners_data.name: Willewonga
runners_data.note: Prominent style but pulled up twice recently including here last year at 50-1
runners_data.comment: Pulled up at Cheltenham last month but after a break; might not be a forlorn hope each-way
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up at 50-1 in this last year and same outcome at the Cheltenham Festival last month, when 100-1; however, that latest outing was his first run for 110 days and he may have needed it; in front when making a bad blunder at the final fence at Bangor (3m, soft) last February and that form suggests he might not be a forlorn hope each-way, at what should be a big price.

runners_data.name: Take All
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse perfectly suited to expected race shape, headgear and wind op applied
runners_data.comment: Ran well for a long way at Cheltenham; could have an each-way shout now back down in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Good efforts in defeat behind Java Point (3m, good to soft) and Unexposed Party (2m6f, good to soft) this year and ran well for a long way before fading at last month's Cheltenham Festival (3m2f); could have an each-way shout at big odds now back down in trip; reapplied cheekpieces replace hood.

runners_data.name: Joker De Mai
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 48-day break after Chair fall here last year
runners_data.comment: Caught the eye two starts ago but he needs to step up on this season's handicap form
runners_data.spotlight: 7-1 when early faller at the Chair in this last year; this 7yo was an eye-catching third at Ludlow in February on penultimate start, having been hampered, but needs to step up on this season's handicap form if he's to threaten.

runners_data.name: Lets Go Champ
runners_data.note: Prominent style with excellent recent form, won last time at Gowran Park
runners_data.comment: Beat a very solid yardstick for last month's hunter chase win and firmly in calculations
runners_data.spotlight: Won a competitive handicap chase at the Punchestown festival in May 2024 for Henry de Bromhead (2m4f, good to yielding) and winning a hunter chase at Gowran Park (3m1f, heavy) last month showed that he retains considerable ability at the age of 11; firmly in calculations.

runners_data.name: Gracchus De Balme
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won this in 2023, pulled up at Cheltenham last time
runners_data.comment: Pulled up at Cheltenham Festival but won this last year and he's capable of bouncing back
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up at the Cheltenham Festival (3m2f, good to soft) last month; however, he was also pulled up at Leicester last February prior to winning this race at 22-1 (good to soft) so he's capable of bouncing back.

runners_data.name: Empire De Maulde
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with moderate recent form, headgear first time
runners_data.comment: Four point wins last year but this 12yo hasn't shone in 2026
runners_data.spotlight: Four point wins last year and runner-up in two hunter chases last spring (2m7f/2m6f, good to soft/good); however, he'll need to improve upon that form and this 12yo hasn't shone on either outing this year.

runners_data.name: Enqarde
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits race shape but pulled up last time at Exeter
runners_data.comment: 50-1 winner at Leicester in February but pulled up at Exeter since; probably vulnerable
runners_data.spotlight: Career highlight was the Tommy Whittle at Haydock in 2021; 50-1 winner of four-runner hunter chase at Leicester (2m6f, soft) this February but pulled up at Exeter (3m, good to soft) since; this 12yo is probably vulnerable.

runners_data.name: Fan De Blues
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 43-day break, headgear first time
runners_data.comment: Very useful in his prime; not devoid of promise for this yard but needs a step forward
runners_data.spotlight: Very useful for Willie Mullins and ran pretty well over these fences in the 2023 Topham; following a long absence this 11yo hasn't been devoid of promise for his new yard, but needs to take a significant step forward.

runners_data.name: Music Drive
runners_data.note: Prominent style with good Cheltenham Festival form, headgear and wind op
runners_data.comment: Again made the frame at 33-1 in the Cheltenham Festival hunter chase; each-way contender
runners_data.spotlight: He's made the frame at 33-1 in the last two runnings of the Cheltenham Festival hunter chase, finishing about 8l behind Barton Snow and Its On The Line last month when third; tackles a new track today and the drop back in trip isn't an obvious positive, but he could still be an each-way contender.

runners_data.name: Golden Son
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with easy hunter chase wins this year, Paul Nicholls stable in form
runners_data.comment: 14l fourth at Cheltenham last month; work to do but the drop back in trip may help
runners_data.spotlight: Useful handicapper who posted easy wins this year in his first two hunter chases (3m/2m7f, good to soft/heavy); 14l fourth at the Cheltenham Festival last month (3m2f, good to soft) so has work to do with some of these, but he was left behind up the hill and is not ruled out back down in trip.

runners_data.name: Unexpected Party
runners_data.note: Prominent style with top-class form, 54 days since last run may be issue
runners_data.comment: Comfortable wins over 2m5f/2m6f on last two starts; holds leading form claims
runners_data.spotlight: Won the Grand Annual at Cheltenham Festival in March 2024 (2m, soft) and runner-up in it last year (good to soft); comfortable wins in hunter chases on last two starts (2m5f/2m6f, good/good to soft); his stamina will be more severely tested in today's hotter company but leading claims if seeing it out.

runners_data.name: Barton Snow
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with perfect 5-5 record in hunter chases, won Cheltenham last time
runners_data.comment: Won the big one at Cheltenham last month; should be fine back down in trip; major player
runners_data.spotlight: Proved his stamina and made it 5-5 under rules (all in hunter chases) when beating Its On The Line by a neck to win the big one at Cheltenham (3m2f, good to soft) last month, despite a mistake at the final fence; has also won on good going; he doesn't appear to be straightforward but clearly knows how to win and should be fine back down in trip; major player.

runners_data.name: A Moments Madness
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner will dictate terms, progressive form but big class rise
runners_data.comment: His comeback third at Carlisle can be upgraded; could go well at sizeable odds
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive in handicap chases last spring for Warren Greatrex (2m2f/2m3f, good/soft) and last month's third on stable debut in a hunter chase at Carlisle (2m5f, good to soft), after an absence, can be upgraded as he hung left at that right-handed track; has plenty to find but this 7yo is very lightly raced and, now going left-handed, could go well at sizeable odds.

runners_data.name: Snipe
runners_data.note: Hold-up style ideally suited to race shape, won last hunter chase start at Hereford
runners_data.comment: 2-3 in hunter chases but he needs a clear career best if he's to win this
runners_data.spotlight: Won on his first hunter chase start at Hereford (2m5f, soft) in January and bounced back from a heavy defeat behind Golden Son at Taunton (2m7f, heavy) to win at Leicester (2m, good to soft) last month; however, he needs a clear career best if he's to win this.

runners_data.name: Great Notions
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid form, good value at likely big odds
runners_data.comment: Some good runs in defeat in handicaps since November but plenty to find today
runners_data.spotlight: Won maiden hunter chase at Hexham (3m, good) last May; some good runs in defeat in handicaps since November, most recently 5l second at Sedgefield (3m2f, good), but he has plenty to find today.

runners_data.name: Famous Clermont
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from long 314-day absence, won this in 2023
runners_data.comment: Won this in 2023 but this 11yo probably isn't as good as he once was; others are preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Won this in 2023 (good to soft) and bagged further hunter chase wins in the same Stratford race in May 2024 and 2025 (2m6f, good); won a point last month and he's better than he showed when tailed off in this last April, but this 11yo probably isn't as good as he once was and others are preferred.

runners_data.name: Fairly Famous
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong Cheltenham hunter chase wins, 314-day break concerning
runners_data.comment: In good heart in points but last May's hunter chase form suggests he's up against it
runners_data.spotlight: Strong form when winning hunter chases at Cheltenham in May 2023 and May 2024; in good heart in point-to-points this season but last May's hunter chase form suggests he may be found wanting.

runners_data.name: A Jet Of Our Own
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who finished fifth in this race last year at huge odds
runners_data.comment: Hard to fancy on this year's form but ran well when fifth of 29 at 125-1 in this last term
runners_data.spotlight: Very hard to fancy judged on this year's hunter chase form but he took a big step forward when fifth of 29 at 125-1 in this race last April (good to soft) and is not ruled out each-way back over these obstacles.

runners_data.name: Densworth
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with inconsistent recent form, well beaten in handicaps
runners_data.comment: The odd snippet of useful form in 2024 but down the pecking order on subsequent evidence
runners_data.spotlight: Showed the odd snippet of very useful form in 2024, winning easily at Wetherby (2m3f, good) that November on his second chase start; however, his subsequent exploits put him well down the pecking order in this line-up.

runners_data.name: Hollywood Harmon
runners_data.note: Prominent runner carrying 7lb less than rivals, won maiden hunter chase
runners_data.comment: Won maiden hunter chase at Cartmel last May but she would be a shock winner today
runners_data.spotlight: Easily won a maiden hunter chase at Cartmel (2m5f, good to soft) last May; didn't run badly at Fakenham (3m, soft) in February but well beaten at Carlisle (2m5f, good to soft) since and she would be a shock winner.

runners_data.name: Whats The Solution
runners_data.note: Prominent runner making hunter chase debut, good point-to-point form
runners_data.comment: Ran okay last May in his sole hunter chase but looks up against it today
runners_data.spotlight: 6-21 in points, his latest win in that sphere coming last month; 12l third of six to Barton Snow at Stratford (2m6f, good) last May in his sole hunter chase and he looks up against it.

races.paceDynamic: A Moments Madness is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 25-runner field, meaning he'll get his own way in front without early pressure. Behind him, 10+ runners want prominent positions including Its On The Line, Barton Snow, Unexpected Party, Golden Son and Music Drive, creating a bunched pack tracking the leader. This congestion will cause traffic problems and interference from 3 out as the field narrows, with many prominent runners getting squeezed for room. The sustainable early pace followed by late carnage strongly favours hold-up horses who can pick their way through the chaos and hit the line late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Heroes Strike
scenarios.trigger: If A Moments Madness sets moderate fractions and the prominent pack gets snarled up turning for home
scenarios.body: The patient riders with space to maneuver will capitalize as the congested front group falls apart in the final half-mile. Thunder Rock, Barton Snow and Take All are perfectly positioned to exploit the inevitable traffic problems.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Position Pays
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners sort themselves out cleanly and avoid major interference
scenarios.body: The class horses tracking just behind A Moments Madness maintain their positions and battle it out up the straight without getting caught in trouble. Its On The Line and Unexpected Party have the quality to prevail if they stay clear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If A Moments Madness goes too slow and gets swamped by the prominent brigade before halfway
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish with all styles converging together, turning it into a pure class contest. Barton Snow's proven stamina and recent Cheltenham win give him the edge in a tactical affair.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Carnage Creates Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers and interference eliminate the market leaders
scenarios.body: The race opens up for an unfancied runner who avoids trouble and stays on their feet through the chaos. A Moments Madness could even steal it if he's still there at the business end with the field decimated behind him.

watchPoints.text: A Moments Madness must be monitored early - if he goes too slow the prominent pack will swamp him before halfway
Traffic problems will develop from 3 out as 10+ prominent runners converge - watch for interference and fallers
Thunder Rock and other hold-up horses positioned at the back - track their moves from 2 out as the race develops
Barton Snow's jumping and positioning crucial given his hold-up style in such a large field
First-time headgear on Java Point, Music Drive, Empire De Maulde and Fan De Blues could spark improvement

races.name: William Hill Aintree Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: El Fabiolo
runners_data.note: Lone front runner returning to hurdles after chasing problems, will dictate terms but lacks recent competitive racing
runners_data.comment: Latest win took hurdles record to 4-7; the best horse in this if viewed on peak chase form
runners_data.spotlight: Probably acts on any going; high class over fences until jumping issues developed; has proved suited by the return to hurdles and an easy win at Leopardstown (2m2f) last time took his record in this sphere to 4-7; the best horse in this field if viewed on his peak chase form.

runners_data.name: The New Lion
runners_data.note: Progressive prominent racer from top yard, ran well in Champion Hurdle and trip extension should suit
runners_data.comment: Ran well in the Champion Hurdle; leading novice at about 2m4f last term; commands respect
runners_data.spotlight: Broadly progressive; has gone down the Champion Hurdle route this season and ran well in that race most recently, while leaving the impression he's ready for a return to further than 2m; leading novice hurdler at about 2m4f last term, winning the Challow and the Turners (both on good to soft ground); still unbeaten over this sort of distance and commands respect.

runners_data.name: Lucky Place
runners_data.note: Reliable prominent runner but disappointing at Cheltenham, needs to bounce back from poor Festival run
runners_data.comment: Still needs to prove he's a Grade 1 hurdler and has the worst chance at the weights
runners_data.spotlight: Went for a handicap option at the latest Cheltenham Festival and was well beaten, albeit with the race not panning out totally smoothly; dual Grade 2 winner last term but still needs to prove he's a Grade 1 hurdler and has the worst chance at the weights in this field.

runners_data.name: Alexei
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with good strike-rate this season, headgear applied suggests connections want improvement
runners_data.comment: Good strike-rate; ran well in the Champion Hurdle and remains a progressive sort
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on any ground; good strike-rate includes wins in the Greatwood and Kingwell this season; ties in with Brighterdaysahead and The New Lion on Champion Hurdle running where a late blunder cost him ground when challenging for the places; has form at up to 2m3f; remains a progressive sort.

runners_data.name: Golden Ace
runners_data.note: Lucky Champion Hurdle winner carrying 7lb penalty, exposed as fortunate and beaten by today's rivals recently
runners_data.comment: Registered her Grade 1 wins in fortuitous fashion and is going to need further luck
runners_data.spotlight: Fortuitous winner of the 2025 Champion Hurdle (same story in the Fighting Fifth) and finished only fifth, behind some of today's rivals, when attempting to retain her crown; largely consistent and has won over 2m4f but increasing her Grade 1 tally may require further luck.

runners_data.name: Brighterdaysahead
runners_data.note: High-class prominent racer with excellent going record, most dangerous if race becomes tactical
runners_data.comment: Very smart mare; easy winner at this meeting in 2024; has leading claims at the weights
runners_data.spotlight: Has form on most types of ground; took her Cheltenham Festival record to 0-3 with a defeat in the latest Champion Hurdle but that was a respectable effort without managing to confirm placings with Lossiemouth, who had played second fiddle in the Irish equivalent; record of 2-3 at about 2m4f includes an easy success in the Mersey at this meeting two years ago; very smart mare who holds leading claims at the weights.

runners_data.name: Potters Charm
runners_data.note: Freshest contender having skipped Cheltenham, prominent style suits but 46 days off is lengthy for hurdles
runners_data.comment: Record of 7-11 over hurdles; 1-1 at Aintree (Gr 1 novice) and he's the freshest contender
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on any ground; the freshest contender in this race, having bypassed the Cheltenham Festival and been absent since landing the National Spirit at Fontwell (2m3f) over six weeks ago when taking hurdles record to 7-11; sole attempt at Aintree resulted in a Grade 1 novice success on Boxing Day 2024; likely to go well.

races.paceDynamic: El Fabiolo will lead from the start with no other natural front runners in this field. The New Lion, Lucky Place, Alexei, Golden Ace, Brighterdaysahead and Potters Charm will all settle in behind, creating a bunched pack stalking the leader. With El Fabiolo able to dictate uncontested fractions over 2m4f, this sets up perfectly for prominent racers who can track the pace and have enough left to mount a challenge. The lack of pace pressure and small field size strongly favours horses who can travel well in behind and finish - the prominent runners hold all the tactical cards here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop Suits
scenarios.trigger: If El Fabiolo maintains steady fractions without getting headed early
scenarios.body: The pace will be honest but not punishing, allowing the classier prominent racers to travel smoothly and time their challenges perfectly. This plays directly into the hands of horses like The New Lion and Brighterdaysahead who thrive when able to pick off a lone leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If El Fabiolo finds another gear turning for home and opens up a decisive advantage
scenarios.body: The front runner's superior stamina and fitness from recent racing could prove decisive if he can stretch the field. With only seven runners and good ground conditions, a bold front-running performance becomes very dangerous to peg back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes very sedate and turns into a sprint finish
scenarios.body: A slowly-run race would favour the horse with the most natural speed and class, allowing superior ability to shine through. Golden Ace and Brighterdaysahead have shown they can quicken sharply when the tempo lifts late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses try to improve position simultaneously approaching the final flight
scenarios.body: With so many prominent racers bunched together, interference or a false pace could create a messy finish. This type of scramble often suits the most experienced campaigner who can find gaps.

watchPoints.text: El Fabiolo could steal this if allowed uncontested lead and his jumping holds up under pressure
Watch for traffic problems in small field if multiple horses improve position simultaneously at final flight
Golden Ace needs to prove Champion Hurdle win wasn't just fortune after being exposed since
Lucky Place must bounce back immediately from poor Cheltenham run or confidence could be shot
Potters Charm's freshness advantage versus 46-day layoff will be telling in final furlong

races.name: Close Brothers Red Rum Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Inthepocket
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with good headway at Cheltenham before falling, suits the likely tactical scenario but form mixed over fences
runners_data.comment: Made headway in the Grand Annual prior to falling two out; his finest hour came here
runners_data.spotlight: His fortunes over fences have been mixed but he made good headway in the Grand Annual at Cheltenham (2m, good) last month prior to falling two out; finest hour came when winning Grade 1 Top Novices' Hurdle here (2m, good to soft) in April 2023; could have a big say if avoiding mishap.

runners_data.name: Hercule Du Seuil
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs strong pace to be effective, below par on last two winter starts but has Grade 3 form
runners_data.comment: Ex-Willie Mullins; won Grade 3 chase last May but hard to fancy on more recent evidence
runners_data.spotlight: Won Grade 3 at Killarney (2m4f, yielding) last May for Willie Mullins and he's on a handy mark on that form; however, below par in the winter on final two starts for that yard and soundly beaten in handicaps on both outings for this stable; usual hood is left off; needs to get back on track.

runners_data.name: Boothill
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making Aintree debut after wind surgery, Ascot specialist but track inexperience is concern
runners_data.comment: 8th in the Grand Annual and 4lb lower today, but this 11yo needs to find something extra
runners_data.spotlight: Ascot specialist who runs at Aintree for the first time; following wind surgery he ran okay when 13l eighth of 20 in the Grand Annual at Cheltenham (2m, good) last month, and he's another 4lb lower today; however, this 11yo is without a win since 2023 and needs to find something extra now in cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Javert Allen
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits the pace scenario, fourth course-and-distance on reappearance suggests he handles the track
runners_data.comment: Below par last time but in good form otherwise this season and could make a bold bid
runners_data.spotlight: Below par at Kempton (2m4f) in February last time but he's run well in defeat otherwise this season, including when fourth over C&D (good to soft) on his reappearance in a race that worked out extremely well; this front-runner could make a bold bid in first-time cheekpieces back at 2m.

runners_data.name: Grain d'Oudairies
runners_data.note: Progressive prominent runner with 52 days off, won twice this season but limited racing for his age
runners_data.comment: 10yo who has enjoyed a progressive season but this may prove too competitive
runners_data.spotlight: 10yo who hasn't had much racing for his age and has been progressive this term, with wins at Kelso (2m1f, good to soft) and Haydock (2m4f, good to soft); however, below par at Carlisle in February last time and, even if back on song, there's a firm suspicion this will prove too competitive.

runners_data.name: Sans Bruit
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner who has won this race twice in April, 81 days off but previous course-and-distance wins suggest he holds the key
runners_data.comment: Has won last two runnings of this race; did it comfortably last year when just 3lb lower
runners_data.spotlight: His exploits earlier in the season aren't of much concern given his last five wins have come in the month of April, including the last two runnings of this race (soft/good to soft; has also won on good); this prominent racer did it comfortably 12 months ago and is just 3lb higher today; could once more take all the beating.

runners_data.name: Stencil
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who impressed at Chepstow in January, 28 days off and good recent Cheltenham effort despite being tailed off
runners_data.comment: 5yo who ran better than the bare facts at Cheltenham; interesting now back down in trip
runners_data.spotlight: 5yo; trained in France but campaigned in Britain since start of 2025; impressed in a warm novice chase at Chepstow (2m, soft) in January and 25l tenth in the Jack Richards at Cheltenham (2m4f, good) was better than the bare facts, as he pulled hard and was held up in a race that favoured those who were up with the pace; could settle better now back down in trip; interesting.

runners_data.name: Highlands Legacy
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with 81 days absence, won last time at Windsor but needs strong pace to be effective
runners_data.comment: Enjoying a progressive first campaign over fences; every chance he'll continue to improve
runners_data.spotlight: Won on chase debut at Worcester (2m, good) in October and runner-up on next two starts (including C&D) before narrow win at Windsor (2m, soft) in January; he's 6lb higher than last time and in a hotter race today, but this progressive 7yo may be able to find the necessary further improvement.

runners_data.name: Jasko Des Dames
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who returned to form at Cheltenham, led jumping two out at Festival showing tactical speed
runners_data.comment: Led jumping 2 out in the Grand Annual (when 5th); this less demanding track could be ideal
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to form back on better ground when fifth, beaten just over 10l, in the Grand Annual at Cheltenham (2m, good); he led jumping two out at the Festival and this less demanding track could be right up his street.

runners_data.name: Dr T J Eckleburg
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse running off 10lb lower mark than last year's fifth, 47 days off but hasn't shown enough recently
runners_data.comment: 10lb lower than when fifth in this last year but others arrive with more pressing claims
runners_data.spotlight: Runs off a mark 10lb lower than when fifth of 14 in this last year, beaten just over 13l; he's run a couple of reasonable races this season but hasn't shown enough to suggest he's the one to be on today.

runners_data.name: Ryan's Rocket
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer dropping back in trip after weakening over 2m4f, November handicap win shows his ability
runners_data.comment: Firmly in the picture on his November win but his jumping might be put under pressure here
runners_data.spotlight: Firmly in the picture judged on his handicap win at Newbury (2m, good to soft) in November and he drops back in trip today having weakened over 2m4f at Kempton last month; not ruled out but he made mistakes last time and has unseated on two of his last four starts; needs to cut out the blunders.

runners_data.name: Brookie
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with concerning recent form including Champion Chase tailed off effort, hard to assess current ability
runners_data.comment: Hard to say what sort of form he's in but this C&D brought out very best in him last April
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up in Ascot handicap in November and tailed off on sole outing since in the Champion Chase last month; it's hard to say what sort of form he's in but this C&D brought out the very best in him when runner-up in the Grade 1 Maghull Novices' Chase (good) 12 months ago; could go well back here.

runners_data.name: Wonleg
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with 104 days absence, returned to form in December but needs career-best to win this
runners_data.comment: Unexposed 6yo who represents a top Irish trainer and may yet have more to offer
runners_data.spotlight: Won Wexford handicap (2m, good) last July on third chase start and returned to form when third of 20 at Leopardstown (2m1f, yielding) in December; needs a career best today but this unexposed 6yo represents a top Irish trainer (who saddles three) and could yet have more to offer.

runners_data.name: Petit Tonnerre
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who was ninth in this race last year, recent form poor but won big handicap previously
runners_data.comment: Tailed off on his last three starts but not discounted in view of last May's Irish win
runners_data.spotlight: Soundly beaten ninth in this 12 months ago (good to soft) and tailed off on his last three starts; however, the return to better ground can help and he won a big-field handicap at Punchestown (2m, yielding) last May; on a handy mark judged on that Irish form and he's not discounted.

runners_data.name: Palamon
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with just 9 days off, won convincingly at Bangor with tongue-tie reapplied suggesting improvement
runners_data.comment: Well backed when returning to form with ready win at Bangor; not ruled out off 9lb higher
runners_data.spotlight: Well-backed, even-money favourite at Bangor (2m4f) last Tuesday, when reverting to good ground in a reapplied tongue-tie and returning to form with a convincing win; 9lb higher in a much hotter race today but not ruled out for his top yard on the back of that stylish success.

races.paceDynamic: Sans Bruit will lead from the start with his confirmed front-running style, but as the sole pace-setter he'll face no pressure and can dictate a sustainable gallop. The prominent runners like Inthepocket, Javert Allen, and Grain d'Oudairies will track just behind, while the large contingent of hold-up horses including Hercule Du Seuil, Boothill, Stencil, and Highlands Legacy will be anchored towards the rear. With only one leader setting an uncontested pace over this sharp 2m trip, the race will develop into a sprint finish where horses need to be handy turning in. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and front-runners who can stay close to the pace without having to make up significant ground late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Sans Bruit gets his own way out front and maintains his April record
scenarios.body: The confirmed front-runner faces no pace pressure and can time his effort perfectly, exploiting his proven course-and-distance form in this exact race. His two previous wins in this contest show he has the tactical speed to respond when challenged up the run-in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly dawdling and prominent horses can stalk perfectly
scenarios.body: Inthepocket or Javert Allen can position ideally behind the uncontested leader and have first run when the pace lifts. Their prominent style allows them to avoid the traffic problems that will affect the hold-up brigade when the sprint develops.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Powers Through
scenarios.trigger: If Sans Bruit sets a genuinely strong pace despite lack of pressure
scenarios.body: The early gallop becomes searching enough to set up a late charge from the back, with Hercule Du Seuil or Boothill having the class to reel in tiring leaders. However, they need significant pace collapse to be effective over this sharp track.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Improver Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the race becomes a tactical crawl followed by a blanket finish
scenarios.body: Palamon's recent Bangor win on good ground with the tongue-tie reapplied suggests Dan Skelton has found the key, allowing him to outpace higher-rated rivals. The light weight and in-form connections provide the edge in a tight finish.

watchPoints.text: Sans Bruit's jumping - any mistake from the lone leader will completely change the race dynamic and hand advantage to prominent trackers
Early pace judgment - if Sans Bruit goes too slowly it negates the distance concerns for hold-up horses like Hercule Du Seuil
Inthepocket's position turning in - needs to be handy to use his tactical speed but has shown tendency to get outpaced in competitive handicaps
Prominent runners bunching behind Sans Bruit - traffic problems likely if Javert Allen, Grain d'Oudairies and Inthepocket all converge
Hold-up horses getting into contention - Boothill and Hercule Du Seuil need to be closer than usual given the likely uncontested pace

races.name: Goffs Nickel Coin Mares' Standard Open National Hunt Flat Race (Grade 2) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Divine Diva

runners_data.name: Fairy Park

runners_data.comment: Irish point winner; fared best of the rest behind unbeaten Princess Day at Newbury
runners_data.spotlight: Easily justified favouritism in an Irish point and fared best of the rest behind Princess Day at Newbury (good to soft); could go well, albeit unlikely to reverse placings with that rival who remains unbeaten.

runners_data.name: Ti'mamzel

runners_data.name: It Would Be You
runners_data.note: Promising hold-up type stepping up significantly in class but interesting 4lb weight allowance could help
runners_data.comment: Well on top at Catterick and looks an interesting prospect for Jennie Candlish
runners_data.spotlight: Well on top at the finish in Catterick event (good) and looks an interesting prospect for Jennie Candlish; goes into much deeper waters but could make waves with significant progress possible after one run.

runners_data.name: Martini Majesty
runners_data.note: Hold-up style fits but Alan King stable running below par and her Ascot form looks modest for this grade
runners_data.comment: Ascot scorer who should progress and helps to give Alan King an interesting hand
runners_data.spotlight: Related to a very notable Flat stayer for her yard; it's hard to get excited about the form of her Ascot win (good to soft; beat One Dimensional by 2l) but she should be capable of progress and helps to give Alan King an interesting hand.

runners_data.name: Billey Shiftit
runners_data.note: Poor recent form and hold-up style won't overcome class deficit against this quality field
runners_data.comment: Brings the worst form having finished only sixth at Wincanton
runners_data.spotlight: Brings the worst form having finished only sixth of 14 in Wincanton contest; may do better in due course but this looks an impossible task.

runners_data.name: Peace Belle
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner but looks outclassed despite yard also running the more promising It Would Be You
runners_data.comment: Won at Hexham then not disgraced at Newcastle; this is much harder
runners_data.spotlight: Far from disgraced at Newcastle when carrying a penalty for her Hexham success; however, looks well short of Graded standard; yard also runs It Would Be You.

runners_data.name: Brave Lady
runners_data.note: 250 days absence is major concern despite Derek O'Connor's ability and her previous Galway festival promise
runners_data.comment: Absent since showing promise with third of 15 at last year's Galway festival
runners_data.spotlight: Absent since showing promise with third of 15, one place behind Midnight Musical, at last year's Galway festival (on good ground); open to improvement but this presents a demanding return to action.

runners_data.name: Burds Of A Feather
runners_data.note: Front-running style dangerous in this pace scenario but tongue-tie first time could help settling
runners_data.comment: Fizzy sort but has potential; wasn't for catching at Warwick on rules debut
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 2-2 in completed starts, namely wide-margin wins on final attempt in Irish points and on rules debut; went freely to post and in the race at Warwick (soft) but wasn't for catching, having soon established a clear lead; withdrawn when 4-1 for Sandown Listed event since, having bolted before the start; has potential provided her fizzy ways can be tamed.

runners_data.name: Tiktok Casey
runners_data.note: Lead/prominent style risky given pace setup but her heavy ground credentials are rock-solid for conditions

runners_data.spotlight: Irish mare who has belied 20-1 and 28-1 odds since switched to rules, rallying to win at Naas (soft to heavy) then good third in Grade 2 Leopardstown event at the Dublin Racing Festival (heavy); seems likely to give supporters a good run for their money.

runners_data.name: Nan's Choice
runners_data.note: £115k purchase for Skelton stable brings prominent style that may suit if she can avoid early pace battle
runners_data.comment: Sold for £115,000 since winning by 5l at Gowran Park; has joined Dan Skelton; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: Has a useful pedigree; won by 5l at Gowran Park (heavy) in the latest of her two outings for Conor Houlihan; sold for £115,000 the following week and has joined Dan Skelton; interesting contender, with any amount of further improvement a possibility.

runners_data.name: Emerald Quest
runners_data.note: Another front-runner in dangerous pace scenario but tongue-tie helped last time and yard booking top amateur
runners_data.comment: Had some luck at Huntingdon but breezed clear in the manner of a potentially useful mare
runners_data.spotlight: Avoided trouble and scored easily in an incident-packed race at Huntingdon (soft) with tongue-tie applied on return from lengthy absence; had some luck but breezed clear in a manner that suggests she is potentially useful; one to consider.

runners_data.name: Princess Day
runners_data.note: Unbeaten leader whose class could overcome tactical disadvantage if she can avoid speed duel with Kiltybo
runners_data.comment: Won well at Newbury last time; remains unbeaten and has plausible Graded aspirations
runners_data.spotlight: Remains unbeaten, having won her sole attempt in the Irish point-to-point scene and both starts under rules; beat Fairy Park in great style at Newbury (good to soft) most recently, looking a mare who has plausible Graded aspirations; commands respect.

runners_data.name: Ladies Day
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer whose consistent seconds suggest she finds one too good but lacks winning strike-rate lately
runners_data.comment: Point bumper winner who has consistent rules form; second last time to Ti'mamzel
runners_data.spotlight: Point bumper winner whose consistent rules form has culminated in second-place finishes at Aintree (failed only narrowly) and Huntingdon (Listed; behind Ti'mamzel); again likely to give her running.

runners_data.name: One Dimensional
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits but pedigree suggests she needs obstacles and this flat track may not play to strengths
runners_data.comment: Faces a stiff task and is crying out for jumps races over further
runners_data.spotlight: Has consistent RPRs but faces a much stiffer assignment upped in grade and gives the impression, backed up by pedigree, that she's crying out for jumps races over further.

runners_data.name: Roxy Russet
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner still seeking first win and Charlie Longsdon yard completely out of form this season
runners_data.comment: Ran well behind Seven Stars last time but looks out of her depth at this level
runners_data.spotlight: Ran well behind Seven Stars at Hereford, showing that her fall in the Huntingdon race won by Emerald Quest had left no scars but taking record to 0-3; seems out of her depth at this level.

runners_data.name: Lennon Grove
runners_data.note: Progressive hold-up type whose Sandown third behind Ti'mamzel gives solid form reference for this contest
runners_data.comment: Ran well in the Sandown race won by Ti'mamzel; this Irish mare has progressive RPRs
runners_data.spotlight: Opened her rules account in Thurles event and has since performed well in the Sandown Listed contest (soft) won by Ti'mamzel; this Irish mare brings progressive RPRs, which suggests another good run is likely.

runners_data.name: Seven Stars
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with strong recent Hereford win showing she can capitalize when pace sets up perfectly
runners_data.comment: Likely to build on her Hereford win; related to two mares who were placed in this race
runners_data.spotlight: Justified favouritism at Hereford (good) last time, beating Roxy Russet by 3l and building on a couple of solid efforts; bred to do better still, being related to several winners for her stable, including two mares who were placed in this contest; strong credentials.

runners_data.name: Kiltybo
runners_data.note: Class front-runner whose recent Naas victory posted strong figures but dangerous tactics given multiple pace rivals
runners_data.comment: Has possibilities on the figures but another easy lead is not guaranteed
runners_data.spotlight: Swallowed up in the Thurles race won by Lennon Grove on rules debut but has made all in both starts since and the figure she recorded at Naas (soft to heavy) last time gives her possibilities upped in class; an easy lead isn't as certain back in a bigger field, however.

runners_data.name: Midnight Musical
runners_data.note: Hold-up style fits but maiden status and first-time cheekpieces suggest she's struggling to find winning form
runners_data.comment: Has gone the wrong way since finishing second at Galway; headgear is now applied
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden who has posted a couple of duck eggs since finishing second at the Galway festival on rules debut; first-time headgear needs to have a major effect.

races.paceDynamic: Kiltybo, Princess Day, Burds Of A Feather, Emerald Quest and Tiktok Casey will ensure a relentless gallop from the outset in this 20-runner Grade 2. With five confirmed front-runners all wanting to make the running, the pace will be genuinely strong throughout the 2m1f trip on testing ground. The stamina-sapping combination of soft turf and fierce early tempo will stretch the field dramatically. This race shape heavily favours proven stayers with hold-up tactics who can capitalize on the inevitable pace collapse in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Rewards Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the five front-runners engage in a fierce early battle through testing ground
scenarios.body: The leaders will fold dramatically in the final 3f, allowing patient hold-up horses with proven stamina to sweep past exhausted pace-setters. Ti'mamzel and Seven Stars possess the class and tactical speed to capitalize when the gallop falls apart.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Leader Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Princess Day or Kiltybo can dictate without getting into an early speed duel
scenarios.body: One class act will use superior tactical awareness to avoid the early burn-up, maintaining enough energy to resist late challengers. Their unbeaten records suggest tactical maturity beyond their years.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Suits Mudlarks
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground deteriorates further and becomes energy-sapping
scenarios.body: The combination of testing conditions and strong pace will favor horses with proven soft-ground form who can grind out victories. Tiktok Casey's heavy ground win and Ti'mamzel's perfect soft record become decisive factors.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise From Mid-Division
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is even more suicidal than expected with all leaders stopping
scenarios.body: A mid-division runner with tactical pace will find clear daylight as the field concertinas dramatically in the straight. Brave Lady returning from a break could benefit from the carnage ahead.

watchPoints.text: Kiltybo and Princess Day could engage in a suicidal speed battle from the start that destroys both unbeaten records
Burds Of A Feather going freely to post at Warwick suggests she may race too keenly again in this strong pace scenario
Ti'mamzel has never raced beyond 2m1f so stamina for this trip after a fierce gallop remains unproven despite breeding
Divine Diva returning after 145 days needs to show early pace positioning from the Skelton stable to suggest full fitness
Midnight Musical wearing cheekpieces for the first time signals connections expect significant improvement from this maiden
